latin_text: It remains for its perfection and completion to be produced by unity coming from above. God is the unity from which angels draw their being, their life, and all their perfection.
english_translation: It remains for its perfection and completion to be produced by unity coming from above. God is the unity from which angels draw their being, their life, and all their perfection.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico resolves the apparent problem of angelic imperfection: though angels lack self-subsistent being and intelligence, their perfection and completion are "produced by unity coming from above." God is the transcendent source from which angels "draw their being, their life, and all their perfection." [INFERRED] This is not a deficiency but the very structure of creaturely beatitude: the angel's perfection consists in its dependent reception of divine being and illumination.

The philosophical function is soteriological: the dual imperfection is precisely what enables the angel's ascent toward God. A self-sufficient being could not yearn; an angel that lacked nothing would not seek union with God. The very dependence that constitutes imperfection is the dynamism of eternal return. [INFERRED] This explains mystical union: human ascent actualizes this same dependent reception of divine illumination and being.

[INFERRED] Oration (O.1.4) describes mystical union as the soul gathering into itself and receiving divine being. Being & Unity grounds it: participated being is the grace-structure of all creaturely existence.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.TE3.C1.3 | Divine unity as source of angelic perfection
